title: Why Is It Wrong to Sell Your Body? Understanding Liberals’ Versus Conservatives’ Moral Objections to Bodily Markets
authors: Shreyans Goenka; Stijn M.J. van Osselaer
managerial_implications: Moral objections to bodily markets differ by political orientation: exploitation concerns are more salient for liberals, while sanctity concerns are more salient for conservatives. Advocacy and policy communications should address these distinct concerns and distinguish living from deceased bodily products.
agency_assessment: Values-based messages could pressure people when their moral identities are used without balanced information. Preserve deliberation and explain competing considerations.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Impact of Organic Specialist Store Entry on Category Performance at Incumbent Stores
authors: Stijn Maesen; Lien Lamey
managerial_implications: Generalist grocery stores face sales losses after a nearby organic specialist enters. A broader organic assortment, credible specialist brands, and organic feature advertising can improve resilience; frequent deep organic discounts appear less protective. The evidence concerns category performance around observed store entry.
agency_assessment: The abstract studies retail competition and assortment. It does not establish an agency mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Who We Are and How We Govern: The Effect of Identity Orientation on Governance Choice
authors: Jan B. Heide; Simon J. Bell; Paul Tracey
managerial_implications: Governance arrangements should reflect both partners' organizational identities and their interdependence. Apparently compatible identities can conceal different expectations. Managers should diagnose these differences before selecting contractual and relational governance practices.
agency_assessment: The conceptual framework addresses organizational governance rather than individual consumer choice.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Innovation Imprinting: Why Some Firms Beat the Post-IPO Innovation Slump
authors: Simone Wies; Christine Moorman; Rajesh K. Chandy
managerial_implications: Firms that establish a record of breakthrough innovation before an IPO may attract investors willing to support continued innovation. Managers should align the innovation strategy and investor base before listing. Evidence from consumer packaged goods firms supports this explanation of heterogeneous post-IPO innovation trajectories.
agency_assessment: The study concerns corporate innovation and investors; an individual-agency mechanism is not established in the abstract.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Choice Architecture for Healthier Insurance Decisions: Ordering and Partitioning Together Can Improve Consumer Choice
authors: Benedict G.C. Dellaert; Eric J. Johnson; Shannon Duncan; Tom Baker
managerial_implications: Ordering and partitioning insurance options can jointly improve choices when the ordering reflects a reliable consumer model. The same partition can impair discovery if better options sit lower in the list. Validate the ranking objective and preserve access to alternatives.
agency_assessment: Partitioning can restrict effective search without removing formal options. Test customer-relevant ranking quality and the ease of exploring alternatives.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Complaint De-Escalation Strategies on Social Media
authors: Dennis Herhausen; Lauren Grewal; Krista Hill Cummings; Anne L. Roggeveen; Francisco Villarroel Ordenes; Dhruv Grewal
managerial_implications: Active listening and empathy can reduce negative arousal in public social-media complaints, even before the underlying service failure is resolved. Service teams should pair responsive language with actual remediation and track resolution separately from the customer's immediate emotional response.
agency_assessment: Emotional calming could substitute for redress if the firm treats reduced complaint intensity as resolution. Track remedial action and preserve escalation options.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Finding Goldilocks Influencers: How Follower Count Drives Social Media Engagement
authors: Simone Wies; Alexander Bleier; Alexander Edeling
managerial_implications: Influencer engagement has an inverted-U relationship with follower count in the studied campaigns. Reach gains can be offset by weaker perceived relationships. Content customization and brand familiarity change this trade-off, so follower count alone is an incomplete selection criterion.
agency_assessment: Perceived personal relationships can make paid recommendations seem independent. Clear sponsorship disclosure and substantive product information protect evaluation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Learning from Data: An Empirics-First Approach to Relevant Knowledge Generation
authors: Peter N. Golder; Marnik G. Dekimpe; Jake T. An; Harald J. van Heerde; Darren S.U. Kim; Joseph W. Alba
managerial_implications: Research teams can begin with a concrete market phenomenon and purposeful empirical exploration before developing theory. The practical requirement is disciplined measurement and transparent reporting of how patterns were discovered and validated, including the distinction between exploration and confirmation.
agency_assessment: This methods article supplies research guidance rather than a consumer influence mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Nudging App Adoption: Choice Architecture Facilitates Consumer Uptake of Mobile Apps
authors: Crystal Reeck; Nathaniel A. Posner; Kellen Mrkva; Eric J. Johnson
managerial_implications: App adoption responds to the sequence, grouping, color, and wording of choices. Bundling feature decisions can reduce their individual prominence, and wording can imply a default without formally preselecting an option. Evaluate understanding and feature-specific consent alongside onboarding completion.
agency_assessment: Increased adoption may reflect reduced attention to individual permissions. Preserve clear, separable choices and reversible settings.
evidence_basis: Abstract and General Discussion in the retrieved author manuscript, including the active-choice design, habit cues, decision time, and privacy implications; the full statistical analysis has not been independently replicated

title: When and Why Consumers React Negatively to Brand Acquisitions: A Values Authenticity Account
authors: Alessandro Biraglia; Christoph Fuchs; Elisa Maira; Stefano Puntoni
managerial_implications: Acquisitions can damage an acquired brand when customers perceive a loss of its distinctive values. Managers should evaluate value alignment, leadership continuity, brand age, and acquisition communication when assessing integration decisions. The studies support a perceived-authenticity explanation.
agency_assessment: Authenticity language could conceal substantive changes after an acquisition. Communicate actual continuity and change rather than using identity reassurance alone.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Before or After? The Effects of Payment Decision Timing in Pay-What-You-Want Contexts
authors: Raghabendra P. KC; Vincent Mak; Elie Ofek
managerial_implications: In pay-what-you-want settings, asking for payment after delivery can increase payment when experienced product value is high. The effect weakens or reverses at low value. Payment timing therefore requires attention to the experience delivered, including in charitable settings.
agency_assessment: Payment timing may increase felt reciprocity or obligation. Preserve a genuine ability to pay the amount the customer chooses.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Beyond Income: Dynamic Consumer Financial Vulnerability
authors: Linda Court Salisbury; Gergana Y. Nenkov; Simon J. Blanchard; Ronald Paul Hill; Alexander L. Brown; Kelly D. Martin
managerial_implications: Financial vulnerability varies over time and across income groups. Evaluate access to resources, volatility, and exposure to future harm across multiple periods. Income or general financial literacy alone may fail to identify customers who need support.
agency_assessment: A vulnerability framework can guide safeguards. Financial fragility must not become a targeting criterion for harmful commitments.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: A War on Sugar? Effects of Reduced Sugar Content and Package Size in the Soda Category
authors: Kristopher O. Keller; Jonne Y. Guyt
managerial_implications: Soda brands can sometimes reduce sugar while protecting sales. Smaller package introductions perform well on average, while sugar reformulation depends on labeling, branding, and packaging. Evaluate sugar purchased at the category level alongside product sales before describing a health benefit.
agency_assessment: The evidence supports evaluating product and public-health outcomes together; it does not itself establish loss of agency.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Meaning of Manual Labor Impedes Consumer Adoption of Autonomous Products
authors: Emanuel de Bellis; Gita Venkataramani Johar; Nicola Poletti
managerial_implications: Customers who derive meaning from manual tasks may resist autonomous products. Communicating meaningful alternative uses of saved time can improve acceptance. Product teams should also preserve valued manual participation rather than assuming every task is an unwanted burden.
agency_assessment: Meaning-based appeals could override a preference to retain control. Offer genuine manual and automated modes and explain their consequences.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Competition and the Regulation of Fictitious Pricing
authors: Richard Staelin; Joel E. Urbany; Donald Ngwe
managerial_implications: Competition can sustain fictitious comparison prices rather than eliminate them. The article examines disclosure of actual prior prices as a possible remedy. Managers should ground advertised savings in verifiable prices and evaluate whether customers understand the comparison.
agency_assessment: Inflated reference prices can distort deal evaluation. Verifiable price history can support informed comparison.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Bringing the Doctor to the Patients: Cardiology Outreach to Rural Areas
authors: J. Jason Bell; Sanghak Lee; Thomas S. Gruca
managerial_implications: Rural cardiology access depends on physician travel costs, competition, and patient demand. A structural model compares targeted recruitment with subsidies under a physician-supply reduction. Managers can use such allocation models to identify locations at greatest risk, subject to the model's behavioral assumptions.
agency_assessment: The analysis concerns health-service access and constrained resource allocation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Conceptual Contributions in Marketing Scholarship: Patterns, Mechanisms, and Rebalancing Options
authors: Bastian Kindermann; Daniel Wentzel; David Antons; Torsten-Oliver Salge
managerial_implications: Marketing research has increasingly favored introducing and explaining concepts over connecting or debating them. Research managers and editors can broaden evaluation criteria to support useful synthesis and critical comparison. The evidence combines a large article corpus with qualitative interviews.
agency_assessment: This article studies research practices rather than individual consumer influence.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: How High-Arousal Language Shapes Micro- Versus Macro-Influencers’ Impact
authors: Giovanni Luca Cascio Rizzo; Francisco Villarroel Ordenes; Rumen Pozharliev; Matteo De Angelis; Michele Costabile
managerial_implications: High-arousal language increases engagement for micro-influencers but can reduce it for macro-influencers through perceived trustworthiness. Balanced assessments and informative intent can change the response. Campaign evaluation should account for communicator scale and credibility, alongside engagement.
agency_assessment: Arousal and apparent informativity can alter trust without improving evidence about the product. Disclose commercial relationships and verify claims.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Revenue Generation Through Influencer Marketing
authors: Maximilian Beichert; Andreas Bayerl; Jacob Goldenberg; Andreas Lanz
managerial_implications: In the studied direct-to-consumer campaigns, low-followership influencers deliver better endorsement returns than high-followership influencers after costs are considered. Managers should measure the full funnel through sales and endorsement spending, because follower reach alone can misstate economic performance.
agency_assessment: Commercial use of close follower relationships raises a risk when endorsements appear independent. Preserve sponsorship transparency and voluntary choice.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Collaborating to Innovate: Balancing Strategy Dividend and Transactional Efficiencies
authors: Nehal Elhelaly; Sourav Ray
managerial_implications: Supplier collaboration contracts should fit the firm's market positioning and capabilities. Misalignment can reduce innovation performance even when collaboration expands access to knowledge. Contract design therefore requires joint assessment of transaction hazards and the strategy the collaboration is intended to support.
agency_assessment: The study addresses interfirm contracting rather than individual-agency mechanisms.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Targeting Nearby Influencers: The Acceleration of Natural Triadic Closure by Leveraging Interconnectors
authors: Jacob Goldenberg; Andreas Lanz; Daniel Shapira; Florian Stahl
managerial_implications: Connected followers can help a creator reach nearby users more effectively than seeding disconnected high-status influencers. The evidence combines observational studies and a field experiment. Managers should evaluate network position and actual incremental reach, alongside audience size.
agency_assessment: Network proximity may amplify perceived peer endorsement. Make coordinated commercial promotion identifiable and retain user controls over recommendations.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Caring Machine: Feeling AI for Customer Care
authors: Ming-Hui Huang; Roland T. Rust
managerial_implications: AI customer care requires reliable emotion recognition, appropriate responses, and escalation. The conceptual framework links emotional support to both well-being and customer value. Managers should validate those outcomes separately and consult the related correction notice.
agency_assessment: Emotionally responsive agents can create dependence or deflect unresolved complaints. Disclose automation and retain independent escalation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Consequences of Marketing Asset Accountability—A Natural Experiment
authors: Peter Guenther; Miriam Guenther; Bryan A. Lukas; Christian Homburg
managerial_implications: A change in Australian accounting rules provides evidence that marketing-asset accountability can improve long-term marketing efficiency and stock-price informativeness while reducing equity costs. Short-term efficiency and debt-cost effects are less consistent. Financial reporting consequences should be evaluated separately across these outcomes.
agency_assessment: This corporate-reporting study does not establish an individual-agency mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Managing Brand Relationship Plurality: Insights from the Nonprofit Sector
authors: Verena Gruber; Jonathan Deschênes
managerial_implications: Nonprofits can sustain episodic volunteer relationships without continuously intensifying commitment. Distinct recruitment and activation practices can coexist with deeper relationship development. Managers should offer participation forms that match volunteers' desired involvement.
agency_assessment: Respecting non-escalating participation supports a person's control over the intensity of involvement.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Social Profit Orientation: Lessons from Organizations Committed to Building a Better World
authors: Leonard L. Berry; Tracey S. Danaher; Timothy Keiningham; Lerzan Aksoy; Tor W. Andreassen
managerial_implications: Organizations pursuing social benefit need explicit objectives, resources, and implementation practices. Executive interviews identify conditions supporting this orientation across sectors. Managers should measure stakeholder outcomes directly rather than infer social benefit from conventional commercial performance.
agency_assessment: The conceptual and qualitative evidence concerns organizational purpose and social outcomes.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Emotional Energy: When Customer Interactions Energize Service Employees
authors: Julien Cayla; Brigitte Auriacombe
managerial_implications: Customer interactions can regenerate employees' emotional energy when shared attention, mood, autonomy, and status support the encounter. Service managers should consider these features of work design alongside demands for emotional labor.
agency_assessment: The paper emphasizes employee experience and autonomy rather than a demonstrated method of undermining consumer choice.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Enrichment Economy: Market Dynamics, Brand Strategy, and Ethics
authors: Delphine Dion; Roman Pavlyuchenko; and Sonja Prokopec
managerial_implications: Luxury brands operate across primary sales and resale markets in which consumers seek capital gains. Portfolio and relationship decisions should account for resale incentives, market access, and unequal exposure to risk. Ethnographic evidence helps explain how brands sustain these connected markets.
agency_assessment: Investment and status narratives may encourage risky acquisition when resale gains are uncertain. Disclose downside risk and distinguish use value from expected appreciation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Buy Now, Pay Later: Impact of Installment Payments on Customer Purchases
authors: Stijn Maesen; Dionysius Ang
managerial_implications: Installment payments can increase purchase incidence and spending by reducing perceived financial constraints. Evaluate affordability across all commitments and subsequent repayment outcomes alongside retailer sales. The paper combines transaction analysis with experiments on perceived costs.
agency_assessment: Smaller installment amounts can obscure the total obligation. Display total cost and cumulative commitments prominently.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Business-to-Investor Marketing: The Interplay of Costly and Costless Signals
authors: Greg Nyilasy; Shangwen Yi; Dennis Herhausen; Stephan Ludwig; Darren W. Dahl
managerial_implications: Startup pitches benefit from matching language to verifiable resource signals. Passion can help when substantive endowments are present but can backfire when they are absent. Concreteness also has contingent effects. Investors should evaluate supporting evidence separately from rhetorical confidence.
agency_assessment: Pitch language can shift judgments under uncertainty. Verify the substantive resource signals on which the claimed credibility depends.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Race for Data: Utilizing Informative or Persuasive Cues to Gain Opt-In?
authors: Caterina D’Assergio; Puneet Manchanda; Elisa Montaguti; Sara Valentini
managerial_implications: Data-consent messages combine information and persuasive cues in different ways, and those formats affect opt-in. Firms should evaluate understanding and freely expressed consent alongside participation. The observed prevalence of message formats concerns the studied email sample.
agency_assessment: Persuasive consent requests may increase agreement without better understanding. Make data uses, refusal, and withdrawal equally clear.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Sponsored Content as an Epistemic Market Object: How Platformization of Brand–Creator Partnerships Disrupts Valuation, Coproduction, and the Relationship Between Market Actors
authors: Zeynep Arsel; Maria Carolina Zanette; Carolina da Rocha Melo
managerial_implications: Brands and creators face uncertainty about sponsored content's value and production. Knowledge asymmetries can redistribute bargaining power and returns within these partnerships. Managers should make valuation criteria, responsibilities, and information access explicit.
agency_assessment: The abstract establishes partnership asymmetries, but does not directly establish a consumer-agency mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
authors: Stephanie M. Tully; Chiara Longoni; Gil Appel
managerial_implications: Lower AI literacy is associated with greater receptivity partly through perceptions of magic and awe. Adoption metrics may therefore reflect misunderstanding. Managers should evaluate informed adoption and provide understandable explanations of system capabilities and limits.
agency_assessment: Targeting misunderstanding can produce excessive trust. Calibrated explanations and meaningful human alternatives protect choice.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Authenticity in Influencer Marketing: How Can Influencers and Brands Work Together to Build and Maintain Influencer Authenticity?
authors: Barbara Duffek; Andreas B. Eisingerich; Omar Merlo; Guan Lee
managerial_implications: Influencer authenticity depends on how consumers, creators, brands, and agencies interpret the relationship. These expectations can conflict. Partnership management should make creative autonomy, brand fit, and commercial expectations explicit rather than treating authenticity as a single score.
agency_assessment: Apparent authenticity can obscure commercial direction. Sponsorship transparency and truthful product accounts preserve informed evaluation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Immersive Service: Characteristics, Challenges, and Pathways to Consumer Agency
authors: Laurel Anderson; Catharina von Koskull; Martin Mende; Johanna Gummerus
managerial_implications: Services that surround a person's daily life, including residential care, can constrain control through boundaries, roles, competing voices, and protocols. Managers should support residents' voice, meaningful responsibilities, and opportunities to challenge routines. The evidence is an ethnographic account of agency in immersive service.
agency_assessment: Institutional routines and dependence can narrow practical choices even when formal choices remain. Provide effective voice, review, and independent assistance.
evidence_basis: Abstract and managerial implications table in the retrieved published version, including desired agency, service constraints, resident voice, and feasible responsibilities; the qualitative evidence has not been independently recoded

title: Standing Out While Fitting In: Visual Design of Text Overlays in Social Media Communication
authors: Stefania Farace; Francisco Villarroel Ordenes; Dennis Herhausen; Dhruv Grewal; Ko de Ruyter
managerial_implications: Text overlays interact with the underlying image. Large central text combined with dynamic imagery can reduce visual appeal and engagement. Managers should evaluate the complete composition rather than optimize text size, position, and motion separately.
agency_assessment: Attention-capturing layout may make promotional claims more visible than material conditions. Give consequential terms adequate visibility.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Beyond Opt-Out: How Presumed-Consent Language Shapes Persuasion
authors: Romain Cadario; Jenny Zimmermann; Bram Van den Bergh
managerial_implications: Presumed-consent wording can increase behavior even when the formal policy remains opt-in. Endorsement and ownership inferences help explain the response across settings. Evaluate what customers believe has been decided, alongside the legal form of consent.
agency_assessment: Language can imply a decision has already been made. Clearly state the person's ability to decline and avoid fabricated commitments.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Whispers in Your Mind: The Role of Voice Features in Customer Acquisition and Retention
authors: Haifeng Xu; Yi Ding; Yu Ding; Qi Zhang; Cheng Zhang
managerial_implications: Sales-call voice features have different associations with acquisition and retention. The studies identify arousal and perceived competence as relevant mechanisms, while finding no purchase-volume effect. Sales evaluation should distinguish conversion, timing, and purchase volume.
agency_assessment: Vocal arousal and apparent competence can influence trust independently of product quality. Preserve factual explanations and unpressured refusal.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Curating the Crowd: How Firms Manage Social Fit to Stage Social Atmospheres
authors: Ilias Danatzis; Tim Hill; Ingo O. Karpen; Michael Kleinaltenkamp
managerial_implications: Experience businesses shape social atmosphere through customer selection and the management of shared meanings. Ethnographic evidence shows how these practices influence fit and belonging. Managers should assess inclusion and exclusion alongside loyalty and experiential value.
agency_assessment: Belonging and selective admission can create pressure to conform or conceal exclusion. Use transparent access criteria and accessible alternatives.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Too Many or Too Few? Information Cues in Recommender Systems and Consequences for Search and Purchase Behavior
authors: Xing Fang; SunAh Kim; Pradeep K. Chintagunta
managerial_implications: Recommendation information affects both search intensity and efficiency. A field experiment finds the highest sales with one cue, while richer information reduces further exploration. Evaluate match quality and informed comparison alongside conversion.
agency_assessment: Withholding useful comparison information can increase search or sales while making evaluation harder. Keep material attributes accessible.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Measuring Self-Preferencing on Digital Platforms
authors: Lukas Jürgensmeier; Bernd Skiera
managerial_implications: Platform self-preferencing requires a comparison with appropriately similar third-party offerings. Aggregate tests in the studied marketplaces find little evidence, while category and country results vary. Managers and regulators should examine sensitivity to comparison groups and visibility measures before drawing conclusions.
agency_assessment: The paper supplies a diagnostic for potentially biased visibility. Its reported aggregate result must not be described as evidence of pervasive self-preferencing.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Putting Words in Their Mouths: Firm-Generated User Content and Consumer Sharing Behavior
authors: Jonathan M. Beck; Clay M. Voorhees; Paul W. Fombelle; Katherine N. Lemon
managerial_implications: Providing ready-made social posts makes sharing easier but can discourage dissatisfied customers from sharing accounts that conflict with the supplied language. Managers should distinguish participation convenience from representative customer voice.
agency_assessment: Firm-written posts can appear spontaneous and suppress discordant experiences. Permit unrestricted editing and identify commercial assistance.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Increasing Accountability and Compliance with Robot Advice
authors: Jana Holthöwer; Jenny van Doorn; Stephanie M. Noble
managerial_implications: Advice from a robot receives greater compliance when attributed to a human source, through perceived accountability. Social cues can change this response. Evaluate appropriateness and understanding of the advice, and preserve refusal and escalation.
agency_assessment: Perceived obligation to justify refusal can pressure adherence. Ensure advice is warranted and declining it carries no hidden penalty.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Consequences of Bottle Bills: How Bottle Deposit Return Schemes Affect Retail Prices and Lead Consumers to Larger Package Sizes
authors: Kristopher O. Keller; Jonne Y. Guyt
managerial_implications: Bottle deposits can alter retail prices and package-size choices as well as recycling incentives. The New York policy analysis finds price and volume responses concentrated in covered products. Policy evaluation should include substitution across package sizes and operational costs.
agency_assessment: The study evaluates a public policy and substitution patterns; the abstract does not establish an agency-eroding mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Automated Versus Human Agents: A Meta-Analysis of Customer Responses to Robots, Chatbots, and Algorithms and Their Contingencies
authors: Katja Gelbrich; Holger Roschk; Sandra Miederer; Alina Kerath
managerial_implications: Customers' responses to robots, chatbots, and algorithms depend on agent type and task conditions. Findings from one automated-agent category may fail to generalize to another. Deployment decisions should evaluate performance, customer response, and access to human service separately.
agency_assessment: Humanlike presentation may create misplaced trust or conceal automation. Identify the agent and retain meaningful human escalation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Closing the Knowledge Gap: Understanding and Reducing the Environmental Impact of Food Choices
authors: Bart J. Bronnenberg; Trang Bùi; Barbara Deleersnyder; Lesley Haerkens; George Knox; Arjen van Lin; Max J. Pachali; Anna Paley; Robert W. Smith; Samuel Stäbler
managerial_implications: Personalized environmental feedback can improve food-impact knowledge and shift stated choices toward lower emissions. Peer comparisons and category information contribute differently. Managers should track knowledge retention and actual behavior separately from stated choices.
agency_assessment: The intervention supplies information aligned with a stated sustainability objective. Peer comparison and personalization are dual-use mechanisms whose welfare direction depends on implementation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Customers’ Review Content and Their Referral and (Re)Purchase Behaviors
authors: Ruhan Liu; Wanqing Zhang; Pradeep K. Chintagunta
managerial_implications: Writing a review can change the writer's later referral and purchase behavior. Affective and cognitive content produce different responses across the studied settings. Review requests should support honest reflection and measure subsequent behavior without substituting commercially convenient language for the customer's account.
agency_assessment: Shaping the sequence and content of reflection can change subsequent decisions. Allow customers to describe both feelings and reasons in their own words.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Responsible Design Thinking
authors: Minu Kumar; Pietro Micheli; Jatinder Jit (J.J.) Singh; Neil Goldberg
managerial_implications: Design teams can overlook affected stakeholders, environmental consequences, and harms that emerge during rapid prototyping or scaling. Responsible design requires broader inclusion, anticipation of consequences, and governance. Interview evidence motivates these organizational capabilities.
agency_assessment: The article supplies safeguards against design practices that disregard affected people.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: In-Store Advertising with Digital Signage
authors: Dennis Herhausen; David de Jong; Dhruv Grewal
managerial_implications: Field experiments find that in-store digital signage can increase featured-product purchasing, with substantial context dependence and spillovers. Effects vary with product type, placement, and message. Evaluate incremental purchasing and customer outcomes alongside advertising revenue.
agency_assessment: Point-of-choice attention and emotional messaging may encourage purchases without improved product understanding. Preserve clear price and product information.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Leveraging Rational Addiction Theory to Reduce Mobile Usage
authors: Jeeva Somasundaram; Laura Zimmermann; Quang Duc Pham
managerial_implications: Preannounced fixed usage-reduction targets can induce earlier reductions in smartphone use. The trials support a forward-looking habit mechanism with heterogeneous responses. Digital-well-being programs should evaluate sustained usage changes and voluntary goal alignment.
agency_assessment: Habit-based intervention can strengthen self-directed control. The outcome and the customer's chosen goal determine the welfare interpretation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Free Riding on Product Returns to Drive Profits
authors: Elisa Montaguti; Scott Neslin; Sara Valentini
managerial_implications: Returns can influence both future purchases and future returns. Retailers should evaluate these dynamics jointly when choosing marketing spending and return policies. A strict policy that minimizes immediate returns can sacrifice valuable longer-term customer activity.
agency_assessment: The abstract favors evaluating return flexibility and long-run economics; it does not establish a specific agency-eroding mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Customer Data Privacy Stewardship
authors: Jordan W. Moffett; Natalie Chisam; Kelly D. Martin; Robert W. Palmatier
managerial_implications: Responsible privacy management can contribute to customer and firm performance, depending on perceived motives and data risk. Privacy should be assessed as a service commitment with verifiable practices rather than solely as compliance messaging.
agency_assessment: Customer control and credible stewardship can support informed data decisions.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: DICE: Advancing Social Media Research Through Digital In-Context Experiments
authors: Hauke Roggenkamp; Johannes Boegershausen; Christian Hildebrand
managerial_implications: Experiments using entire scrollable feeds can measure contextual spillovers and competition for attention that isolated-post studies miss. Researchers should measure scrolling and recall within the relevant environment and distinguish experimental control from external validity.
agency_assessment: Feed optimization can prioritize sustained attention over users' intentions. Include comprehension, stopping, and user-selected limits in evaluation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: All the News That's Fit to Capitalize: How Person Brands Shape Emergent Markets
authors: Gillian Brooks; Ashlee Humphreys
managerial_implications: Prominent individuals can help emerging markets gain legitimacy through organizational identity, founding narratives, and early audiences. Managers should consider how these assets persist beyond the founding individual while checking the substance behind reputational claims.
agency_assessment: Personal authority and founding narratives may substitute for independent evidence. Preserve verification and the ability to question the spokesperson.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: How E-Scooters Impact Shared Mobility and Consumer Safety
authors: Ruichun Liu; Unnati Narang
managerial_implications: E-scooter entry in the Chicago setting changes demand for other mobility services and is associated with safety and environmental consequences. Managers and policymakers should evaluate substitution and neighborhood heterogeneity alongside operator revenue. The design uses generalized synthetic controls.
agency_assessment: The study concerns mobility and policy consequences rather than an established agency-eroding mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Extended Reality in Business-to-Business Sales: Performance Implications, Adoption Drivers, and Contingency Effects
authors: Janina Mettler; Aline Lanzrath; Christian Homburg
managerial_implications: Extended reality can improve B2B selling by supporting buyers' mental imagery, especially for complex and tactile products. Benefits coexist with possible salesperson stress. Adoption decisions should match the product and selling context and provide support for employees.
agency_assessment: Vivid simulation can create persuasive impressions beyond verified product performance. Distinguish demonstrations from validated capabilities.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Human or AI? Identity Salience Enhances Historically Marginalized (but Not Privileged) Consumers’ Choice of Algorithmic Service Providers
authors: Yeseul Kim; Dipayan Biswas; Courtney Szocs; Khalia Jenkins
managerial_implications: Historically marginalized customers may prefer algorithmic service when identity-based judgment is salient. Automated options can improve access in some nondiverse service settings. Managers should address the source of exclusion while retaining genuine service-channel choice.
agency_assessment: Choice among service channels can protect agency. Steering vulnerable customers into an opaque compulsory channel would reverse that benefit.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Beyond Visibility: The Disability Inclusion Effect in Advertising
authors: Martina Cossu; Zachary Estes; Joachim Vosgerau
managerial_implications: Advertising that meaningfully includes people with disabilities can improve consumer evaluations across several settings. Tokenizing disability or emphasizing impairment weakens the effect. Representation should support agency and inclusion rather than use vulnerability as a promotional cue.
agency_assessment: The studies support representations that preserve agency and avoid tokenization.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Cushioning the Blow: Reducing Customer Attrition in Response to Price Increase Notifications
authors: Hoorsana Damavandi; Kersi D. Antia; Praveen K. Kopalle
managerial_implications: Explanations for price increases affect attrition and perceived switching costs. The storage-provider studies find different responses to market, cost, and quality explanations. Communicate truthful reasons while preserving customers' ability to assess outside options.
agency_assessment: Messages can discourage exit by altering beliefs about alternatives. Provide accurate comparisons and straightforward cancellation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: A Practical Guide to Endogeneity Correction Using Copulas
authors: Yi Qian; Anthony Koschmann; Hui Xie
managerial_implications: Copula approaches can address certain endogeneity problems without conventional instruments, but their validity depends on data and identification conditions. Analysts should check those conditions and model specifications before interpreting adjusted coefficients causally.
agency_assessment: This methods guide does not establish a consumer influence mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Preference Filtering: When Customers Share Narrow Preferences with Algorithms
authors: Phyliss Jia Gai; Eugina Leung; Anne-Kathrin Klesse
managerial_implications: People may report narrower preferences to algorithms because they expect uniform weighting. This can reduce recommendation fit despite appearing rational beforehand. Preference elicitation should explain weighting and permit nuanced revisions.
agency_assessment: An opaque elicitation process can narrow the interests the system recognizes. Enable weighting, correction, and exploration outside the inferred profile.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: EXPRESS: Rethinking Imitation in Marketing Strategy
authors: Suyun Mah; Neil A. Morgan
managerial_implications: Imitation can be a deliberate strategic option with different costs, benefits, and risks across market conditions. Managers should distinguish forms of imitation and compare them with innovation alternatives. The article develops a conceptual framework rather than estimating a universal performance advantage.
agency_assessment: The article concerns firm strategy and does not establish individual agency erosion.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: EXPRESS: Channel Adoption Pathways and Post-Adoption Behavior
authors: Shirsho Biswas; Hema Yoganarasimhan; Haonan Zhang
managerial_implications: Customers' paths into online shopping predict different later spending and channel use. Promotion-induced adoption can involve forward buying and weaker subsequent profitability. Managers should incorporate adoption history when forecasting customer value and promotion returns.
agency_assessment: Inertia is discussed as an explanation of behavior, but the abstract does not establish an intervention that undermines control.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: EXPRESS: The Collecting Mindset: Viewing Purchasing as Collecting Enhances Acquisition Experience and Product Desirability
authors: Elena Bocchi; Adam Eric Greenberg; Zachary Estes
managerial_implications: Positioning a purchase as part of a collection can improve the acquisition experience and product desirability. The effect depends on meaningful progress, active search, and identity fit. Managers should assess whether collecting improves the customer's experience within their intended budget.
agency_assessment: Collection completion and identity can encourage escalating acquisition. Preserve spending visibility and the freedom to leave a collection incomplete.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: How Do Nutritional Warning Labels Affect Prices?
authors: Max J. Pachali; Marco J.W. Kotschedoff; Arjen van Lin; Bart J. Bronnenberg; Erica van Herpen
managerial_implications: Nutrition-warning policies can change firms' prices as well as consumers' preferences. In the Chilean cereal setting, price adjustment reinforces substitution toward healthier products. Evaluate the equilibrium response and effects on price-sensitive households rather than hold all prices fixed when assessing policy.
agency_assessment: Warning labels improve access to consequential information. The welfare interpretation also depends on price responses and consumers' needs.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Product-Harm Crises and Spillover Effects: A Case Study of the Volkswagen Diesel Emissions Scandal in eBay Used Car Auction Markets
authors: Xiaogang Che; Hajime Katayama; Peter Lee
managerial_implications: A product-harm scandal can reduce demand for a firm's unaffected products. Used-car auction evidence shows negative spillovers to compliant Volkswagen models. Crisis management and valuation should account for brand-wide trust effects, while separating these from changes in marketplace participation.
agency_assessment: The study measures reputational spillovers rather than a method of influencing individual agency.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Examining the Efficacy of Time Scarcity Marketing Promotions in Online Retail
authors: Jillian Hmurovic; Cait Lamberton; Kelly Goldsmith
managerial_implications: Time scarcity does not reliably improve online promotions. Context and the explanation for the deadline matter, and favorable effects remain conditional. Managers should verify actual limits and evaluate longer-term decisions, rather than assume urgency improves value.
agency_assessment: Artificial urgency can suppress deliberation. Use genuine deadlines and keep material information available for review.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Daily Me Versus the Daily Others: How Do Recommendation Algorithms Change User Interests? Evidence from a Knowledge-Sharing Platform
authors: Jia Liu; Ziwei Cong
managerial_implications: Moving from content-based to social recommendations changes participation and the concentration of interests in different directions. Platforms should distinguish social-network concentration from topic diversity when evaluating recommendation changes.
agency_assessment: Recommendation rules shape exposure and expressed interests. Give users control over recommendation criteria and access to alternative content.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Effects of Content Ephemerality on Information Processing
authors: Uri Barnea; Robert J. Meyer; Gideon Nave
managerial_implications: Ephemeral content can increase immediate attention, comprehension, and recall by raising concern about missing information. However, customers lose opportunities for later review. Consequential terms should remain accessible even when promotional content is temporary.
agency_assessment: Restricting repeat access can impair later reconsideration and verification despite improved initial attention. Preserve retrievable records.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Favorite Possessions Protect Subjective Well-Being Under Income Inequality
authors: Jingshi (Joyce) Liu; Amy N. Dalton; Anirban Mukhopadhyay
managerial_implications: Attention to favorite possessions can buffer subjective well-being when income inequality is salient by reducing wealth comparisons. Consumer support can emphasize meaningful possessions already owned. The evidence concerns psychological responses, rather than the elimination of material inequality.
agency_assessment: Reducing harmful comparison may support agency. Emotional reassurance should accompany, rather than obscure, consequential material information.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Save More Today or Tomorrow: The Role of Urgency in Precommitment Design
authors: Joseph Reiff; Hengchen Dai; John Beshears; Katherine L. Milkman; Shlomo Benartzi
managerial_implications: The order of immediate and later commitment options changes inferred urgency and saving behavior. Simultaneous offers can weaken perceived urgency, while sequential offers can strengthen it. Evaluate informed commitment and retained flexibility.
agency_assessment: Sequencing can imply urgency beyond the underlying choice. Explain timing consequences and allow deliberate deferral.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: TV Advertising and Online Sales: A Case Study of Intertemporal Substitution Effects for an Online Travel Platform
authors: Anja Lambrecht; Catherine Tucker; Xu Zhang
managerial_implications: TV advertising can bring online browsing and sales forward in time. Very short attribution windows can therefore overstate incremental demand. Evaluate later offsetting declines and channel changes before allocating advertising spending.
agency_assessment: The principal contribution is advertising measurement; the abstract does not establish an agency-eroding intervention.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Effects of Pressure and Self-Assurance Nudges on Product Purchases and Returns in Online Retailing: Evidence from a Randomized Field Experiment
authors: Anindya Ghose; Heeseung Andrew Lee; Kihwan Nam; Wonseok Oh
managerial_implications: Pressure and reassurance can both raise sales, but pressure-oriented nudges generate more product returns in the field experiment. Return-adjusted sales favor a broader evaluation than immediate conversion. Product-fit support can preserve commercial performance while improving decision quality.
agency_assessment: Scarcity and social pressure can prompt purchases later reversed. Measure returns and regret and support informed product-fit assessment.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Impact of Negative Reviews on Online Search and Purchase Decisions
authors: Marton Varga; Paulo Albuquerque
managerial_implications: Negative reviews can change search paths as well as purchase probability, particularly for functional products and complaints about functionality or service. Retailers should diagnose the underlying issue and offer representative review access, rather than interpret a mean rating as sufficient information.
agency_assessment: Selective review visibility can hide information that would change search and purchase. Preserve representative access and clear sorting rules.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Neural Signals of Video Advertisement Liking: Insights into Psychological Processes and Their Temporal Dynamics
authors: Hang-Yee Chan; Maarten A.S. Boksem; Vinod Venkatraman; Roeland C. Dietvorst; Christin Scholz; Khoi Vo; Emily B. Falk; Ale Smidts
managerial_implications: Neural responses during advertisements can improve predictions of subsequent liking and identify differences in response timing. These measures should be validated on new ads and audiences. Predicting liking does not establish persuasion, purchase effects, or welfare consequences.
agency_assessment: Optimizing early affective responses can prioritize attraction over comprehension. Include understanding and informed preference in evaluation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Is It as Bad as It Looks? Judgments of Quantitative Scores Depend on Their Presentation Format
authors: Christophe Lembregts; Jeroen Schepers; Arne De Keyser
managerial_implications: Cumulative versus episode-level score displays can change how people interpret an unusual rating. Cumulative displays may obscure the severity of a deviation. Platforms should provide understandable raw observations and aggregation rules when consequential decisions depend on ratings.
agency_assessment: An aggregation format can distort inference about an underlying episode while displaying numerically correct data. Make both components and averages accessible.
evidence_basis: Abstract and General Discussion in the retrieved full text, including nine experiments, cumulative versus incremental scores, and the distinction between simulated choices and field generalization; no independent replication

title: Soda Taxes and Marketing Conduct
authors: Kristopher O. Keller; Jonne Y. Guyt; Rajdeep Grewal
managerial_implications: Soda-tax responses include changes in promotion frequency, discount depth, and feature advertising. These changes can reinforce sales declines beyond the price effect alone. Policy and brand analyses should model the broader marketing mix and changes in consumer responsiveness.
agency_assessment: This policy evaluation concerns market responses without establishing a distinct agency-eroding mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Response Aggregation to Obtain Truthful Answers to Sensitive Questions: Estimating the Prevalence of Illegal Purchases of Prescription Drugs
authors: Marco Gregori; Martijn G. De Jong; Rik Pieters
managerial_implications: Aggregating responses to paired questions can reduce the burden of disclosing sensitive behavior and improve prevalence measurement. Analysts need the technique's statistical assumptions and should report the inferred population rate rather than identify particular respondents.
agency_assessment: Privacy-preserving measurement can improve participation and truthful reporting. Maintain the distinction between aggregate inference and individual disclosure.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Sunk Cost Effect, Self-Control, and Contract Design
authors: Xing Zhang; Ganesh Iyer; Xiaoyan Xu; Juin Kuan Chong
managerial_implications: Sunk costs can supply desired commitment while reducing flexibility. Optimal contracts depend on consumers' self-control problems and the psychological mechanism. Refundable fees and alternative tariffs change the trade-off.
agency_assessment: A commitment device can become a trap when preferences or circumstances change. Offer understandable terms and appropriate exit or refund options.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Buying Future Endorsements from Prospective Influencers on User-Generated Content Platforms
authors: Andreas Lanz; Jacob Goldenberg; Daniel Shapira; Florian Stahl
managerial_implications: Predicting which new creators will later become influential can support earlier endorsement contracting. The rare-event problem and assumed endorsement returns strongly affect the business case. Managers should validate forecasts and contractual terms before relying on simulated profit potential.
agency_assessment: Early commercial arrangements may be invisible to later audiences. Disclose paid relationships when endorsements occur.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Value of Safety Training for Business-to-Business Firms
authors: Yixing Chen; Shrihari Sridhar; Kyuhong Han; Sonam Singh; Vikas Mittal; Taehoon Im
managerial_implications: Safety training can reduce hazards and injuries and improve how procurement professionals evaluate a supplier. The studies combine quasi-experimental evidence and a stated-choice experiment. Training decisions should track actual safety outcomes alongside commercial benefits.
agency_assessment: The evidence concerns workplace safety and purchasing criteria rather than an agency-eroding mechanism.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Wait for Free: A Consumption-Decelerating Promotion for Serialized Digital Media
authors: Jangwon Choi; Inyoung Chae; Fred Feinberg
managerial_implications: Waiting for free access can expand a serialized content audience and monetize willingness to avoid delay. Revenue gains depend on spillovers and heterogeneity. Evaluate spending transparency and users' ability to stop between episodes.
agency_assessment: Serial access and paid delay avoidance can encourage escalating commitments. Show cumulative cost and support voluntary stopping.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: How Insurance Prices Affect Consumers’ Purchase Decisions: Insurance Price as a Risk Signal
authors: Jochen Reiner; Julia Wamsler; Torsten Bornemann; Martin Natter
managerial_implications: Customers may read an optional insurance price as information about the underlying product's risk. High relative insurance prices can therefore deter the product purchase itself. Provide objective risk information and evaluate the product and insurance offers jointly.
agency_assessment: An insurance price can alter perceived risk without changing objective risk. Clear evidence about coverage and actual failure rates supports informed choice.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Driving Mobile App User Engagement Through Gamification
authors: Jens W. Paschmann; Hernán A. Bruno; Harald J. van Heerde; Franziska Völckner; Kristina Klein
managerial_implications: Game rewards can raise app engagement beyond ordinary rewards, but intensive game involvement may contribute less to the app's substantive activity. Evaluate useful participation separately from time spent and reward pursuit.
agency_assessment: Reward progression can sustain activity after it stops serving the user's objective. Offer limits, pauses, and transparent reward rules.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Who Shares Fake News? Uncovering Insights from Social Media Users’ Post Histories
authors: Verena Schoenmueller; Simon J. Blanchard; Gita Venkataramani Johar
managerial_implications: Past social-media language helps identify misinformation-sharing patterns and design fact-checking interventions. The studies distinguish trait from situational anger and test an intervention encouraging tool adoption. Prediction should be evaluated for error, privacy, and the specific behavior measured.
agency_assessment: Profiles intended for protective intervention could be repurposed to target susceptible users with misinformation. Restrict data use and evaluate protective outcomes.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Last Hurrah Effect: End-of-Period Temporal Landmarks Increase Optimism and Financial Risk-Taking
authors: Avni M. Shah; Xinlong Li
managerial_implications: End-of-period landmarks can increase optimism and financial risk-taking, with worse subsequent returns in the studied lending setting. Financial communication should account for decision timing and assess outcomes beyond immediate participation.
agency_assessment: Time-linked optimism can expose consumers to excessive risk. Provide stable risk information and time to reconsider.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Golden Halo of Defaults in Simple Choices
authors: Nicolette J. Sullivan; Alexander Breslav; Samyukta S. Doré; Matthew D. Bachman; Scott A. Huettel
managerial_implications: Defaults can change attention and valuation in simple choices, including increasing hedonic selection. Effects depend on goals and the type of default. Designers should compare defaulted and active-choice experiences and make alternatives easy to select.
agency_assessment: A preselected option can acquire perceived value beyond its attributes. Transparent defaults and low-cost override preserve control.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Rejections Are Stickier Than Choices
authors: Minzhe Xu; Yang Yang; Chris Janiszewski
managerial_implications: Rejecting alternatives can create more persistent preferences than choosing among them, reducing variety in later decisions. The welfare effect depends on whether the person initially seeks too much or too little variety. Evaluate repeated choice and reconsideration.
agency_assessment: The response task can reshape later preference without changing attributes. Allow alternative framing and revisiting past decisions.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Accounting for Formative and Reflective Topics in Product Review Data for Better Consumer Insights
authors: Joachim Büschken; Thomas Otter; Greg M. Allenby
managerial_implications: Review topics that describe an overall evaluation can be consequences of satisfaction rather than drivers of it. Distinguishing these roles can improve topic coherence and managerial diagnosis. Avoid interpreting every predictive phrase as an actionable product attribute.
agency_assessment: The article improves measurement and interpretation of review text.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Overestimating Stars, Underestimating Numbers: The Hidden Impact of Rating Formats
authors: Deepak Sirwani; Srishti Kumar; Manoj Thomas
managerial_implications: Stars and numeric ratings can generate different systematic magnitude errors. Partial-star rendering and left-digit attention help explain them. Platforms should test comprehension and provide readable underlying values rather than presume familiar formats are neutral.
agency_assessment: Display format can bias evaluation of identical data. Use interpretable scales and make exact values available.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Token-Effort Effect: Trivial Redemption Effort Increases Price Promotion Effectiveness
authors: Kuangjie Zhang; Thomas Allard; Nidhi Agrawal; Rajesh Bagchi
managerial_implications: Very small redemption tasks can increase promotion uptake by creating a favorable perceived return on effort. More demanding tasks do not share that effect. Managers should evaluate participation costs and avoid using nominal effort to distract from the underlying offer.
agency_assessment: A trivial task can change valuation of an unchanged discount. Keep the price comparison clear and participation voluntary.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: How Awe in Marketing Communications Decreases Consumer Preferences for Limited Edition Products
authors: Aysu Senyuz; Jonathan Hasford; Ze Wang
managerial_implications: Awe can reduce demand for limited editions by weakening the desire for exclusivity. Message framing can alter that relationship. Campaign decisions should account for the motive a communication activates rather than assume all positive emotions increase demand.
agency_assessment: Emotion and exclusivity framing can redirect evaluation independently of functional value. Keep scarcity claims truthful and allow deliberation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Rewarding Money or Time? The Sunk Cost Effects of Customized Rewards in Loyalty Programs
authors: Zhigang Shou; Qinying Xia; Samuel Su; Hongxin Teng
managerial_implications: Unexpected rewards for time and money are interpreted differently. Consumers may undercount time costs and treat time-based rewards as windfalls. Loyalty evaluation should include opportunity costs and subsequent spending, alongside redemption and gratitude.
agency_assessment: Reward framing can conceal accumulated effort and encourage further spending. Display time and monetary commitments transparently.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Different Effects of Mass-Media Marketing and Personal Sales Budgets Across the Life Cycle of B2B High-Tech Start-Ups
authors: Arnd Vomberg; Maximilian Friess; Sascha Alavi; Verena Maag; Jan Wieseke
managerial_implications: The association between sales-versus-media spending and performance changes over a B2B startup's life cycle. Personal selling is particularly useful early, while mass media becomes more relevant later. Budget decisions should reflect maturity and the performance measure being pursued.
agency_assessment: The longitudinal evidence concerns organizational resource allocation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: When Words Meet Visuals: How Content Composition Drives Social Media Engagement for Marketer-Generated Content
authors: Ivy Chu Dang; Canice M.C. Kwan; Jayson S. Jia; Yang Shi
managerial_implications: The balance of pictures and overlaid text affects social engagement, with important interactions involving informativeness, placement, emotion, and visual complexity. Evaluate the complete composition and acknowledge the assumptions behind observational causal estimates.
agency_assessment: Visual emphasis can make promotional content salient while material conditions fade. Evaluate comprehension as well as engagement.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Bots Bargaining with Humans: Building AI Super-Bargainers with Algorithmic Anthropomorphization
authors: Sumon Chaudhuri; Arnaud De Bruyn
managerial_implications: Bargaining bots can improve economic outcomes while appearing human, yet damage subjective negotiation experiences. Managers should evaluate relationship consequences as well as immediate gains. Clear agent identity and appropriate negotiation safeguards are essential.
agency_assessment: Humanlike behavior can obscure the counterparty's automated incentives. Disclose automation and preserve recourse and refusal.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: The Weekend Effect in Online Reviews
authors: Andreas Bayerl; Verena Schoenmueller; Jacob Goldenberg; Florian Stahl
managerial_implications: Weekend reviews differ systematically from weekday reviews, partly because different reviewers choose to participate. Review-solicitation timing can therefore change observed ratings. Managers should account for temporal selection before treating score changes as changes in quality.
agency_assessment: Selective solicitation timing can manufacture a more favorable apparent customer experience. Report solicitation practices and maintain representative feedback access.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: A Comparative Analysis of Frontline Employee Wellness Benefits and Customer Responsiveness: A Social Exchange Theory Perspective
authors: Stephanie M. Noble; Dhruv Grewal; Riley T. Krotz; Carl-Philip Ahlbom; Jens Nordfält; Dipayan Biswas
managerial_implications: Some wellness benefits improve frontline responsiveness through feeling valued and indebted. Food and social benefits show stronger effects in the reported studies, especially in supportive workplaces. Managers should evaluate employee well-being directly rather than assume responsiveness fully captures the benefit.
agency_assessment: Indebtedness may turn a benefit into pressure to reciprocate. Keep benefits unconditional and preserve employee voice and reasonable work boundaries.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Improving the Discriminant Validation of Multi-Item Scales
authors: Constant Pieters; Hans Baumgartner; Rik Pieters
managerial_implications: Multi-item scales require evidence that purportedly distinct constructs are empirically distinguishable. The proposed procedure incorporates reliability, measurement error, and sampling error. Analysts should evaluate discriminant validity continuously rather than rely on a convenient binary criterion.
agency_assessment: The article supplies measurement guidance relevant to validating an agency codebook.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Information Disclosure via Platform Endorsement in Online Health Care
authors: Jiajia Zhan; Xu Zhang; Hongqiao Fu
managerial_implications: Platform endorsement can increase paid consultation demand and prices while reducing free provision. The observed quality response differs from the access-equity concern. Health platforms should evaluate information value, provider behavior, and access together.
agency_assessment: An endorsement can be interpreted as neutral advice despite platform revenue incentives. Explain criteria and preserve visibility of suitable alternatives.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Separating the Artist from the Art: Social Media Boycotts, Platform Sanctions, and Music Consumption
authors: Daniel Winkler; Nils Wlömert; Jūra Liaukonytė
managerial_implications: Reduced platform visibility can explain consumption declines that appear to reflect consumer boycotts. Separating playlist removal from intentional audience response changes the interpretation. Managers should identify the source of demand changes before attributing them to values or preferences.
agency_assessment: Platform curation can shape feasible exposure while observed consumption is mistaken for autonomous preference. Provide discoverable alternatives and transparent curation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Market Effects of Inattention: Theory and Evidence from Left-Digit Bias
authors: Andreas Kraft; Raghunath Singh Rao
managerial_implications: Firms can profit from consumer inattention even in competitive used-goods markets. Used-car evidence links odometer left-digit bias to dealer transactions and margins. Customer protection should address how information is interpreted as well as whether it is available.
agency_assessment: Targeting biased interpretation can transfer surplus while formal information remains available. Present comparable quantities and test comprehension.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Consumer Interactions and Peer Effects in Socially Connected Digital Products
authors: Yijun Chen; Yulia Nevskaya
managerial_implications: Peer effects can materially alter retention intervention value in socially connected products. A structural model accounts for endogenous network formation and heterogeneous users. Customer-value calculations should distinguish direct retention value from estimated network spillovers.
agency_assessment: Retention interventions can create social pressure to remain. Preserve independent exit and avoid making peers responsible for another user's participation.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Taking a Stance, for Now or Forever: Optimizing the Communication of Corporate Political Activism
authors: Freeman Wu; Helen van der Sluis; Lauren Grewal; Aradhna Krishna
managerial_implications: Communication permanence can signal commitment to a political stance, with responses depending on audience alignment and other evidence of commitment. Managers should align durable communications with substantive organizational action.
agency_assessment: Identity-aligned commitment signals can win support without equivalent action. Make underlying practices verifiable.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: Gaming the Marketplace: Consumer Opportunism and Beliefs about Societal Hierarchy
authors: Shilpa Madan; Aparna Labroo; Constantine S. Katsikeas
managerial_implications: Beliefs about hierarchy can encourage opportunistic consumer behavior through a desire to feel clever. Surveillance reminders and relationship reminders have different effects. Policy design should examine actual behavior and fairness rather than rely on a single relational appeal.
agency_assessment: Surveillance cues can create compliance pressure and inhibit legitimate claims. Explain monitoring and maintain accessible appeal and return processes.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: EXPRESS: Infinite-Scrolling vs. Pagination: The Impact of Interface Layouts on Product Returns
authors: Huitian Zhang; Lei Su; Jaideep Sengupta
managerial_implications: Infinite scrolling can increase product returns by reducing perceived navigational control and choice closure. Navigation aids and other interventions can mitigate the response. Evaluate returns and control alongside immediate browsing engagement.
agency_assessment: Interface design can reduce control over navigation and later confidence in choices. Provide visible position, stopping points, and easy revisiting.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: EXPRESS: The Humanizing Power of Accents in Voicebots: When Accent-Based Humanization Increases User Engagement
authors: Hesam Ghasemi; Amir Sepehri; Cait Lamberton
managerial_implications: Nonstandard accents can make voicebots seem more human and increase engagement under particular conditions. The effect depends on whether humanization is desired and whether other cues dominate. Managers should preserve accurate agent identity.
agency_assessment: Humanization can encourage unwarranted interpersonal trust in automation. Identify the system and explain what it can and cannot decide.
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract deposited in Crossref; preliminary interpretation

title: When Bulldozers Loom: Informal Property Rights and Marketing Practice Innovation Among Emerging Market Microentrepreneurs
authors: Magda Hassan; Jaideep Prabhu; Rajesh Chandy; Om Narasimhan
managerial_implications: Informal leasing can provide a more secure basis for investment than possession without ownership in the studied Cairo market. Property-right uncertainty can suppress marketing innovation. Programs supporting microentrepreneurs should consider asset security alongside skills and credit.
agency_assessment: The research identifies institutional constraints on entrepreneurial action rather than a consumer persuasion tactic.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Frontiers: Framing Price Increase as Discount: A New Manipulation of Reference Price
authors: Sungsik Park; Man Xie; Jinhong Xie
managerial_implications: A seller can make a price increase appear to be a discount by introducing a list price at the same time. The study documents this practice across tracked online categories. Evaluate actual price histories and consumer understanding rather than the displayed discount alone.
agency_assessment: A reference-price display can reverse the apparent direction of a real price change. Preserve accessible price history and truthful savings claims.
evidence_basis: Publisher or author abstract verified on the primary source page; preliminary interpretation

title: Frontiers: Polarized America: From Political Polarization to Preference Polarization
authors: Verena Schoenmueller; Oded Netzer; Florian Stahl
managerial_implications: Political polarization can extend to brand preferences and purchases. Brands taking a stance may change the composition of their customer base. Managers should measure these shifts across behavior and stated preference without assuming political identity determines every individual decision.
agency_assessment: Political-affinity profiles can be used to substitute identity cues for product evaluation. Limit profiling and provide substantive information.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Mapping Market Structure Evolution
authors: Maximilian Matthe; Daniel M. Ringel; Bernd Skiera
managerial_implications: Dynamic market maps can reveal changes in competitive positioning that static maps obscure. The proposed method uses repeated observations while accommodating noise. Managers can monitor strategic trajectories and validate their interpretation against substantive market changes.
agency_assessment: This analytical method describes competition rather than an agency-eroding mechanism.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Close Enough? A Large-Scale Exploration of Non-Experimental Approaches to Advertising Measurement
authors: Brett R. Gordon; Robert Moakler; Florian Zettelmeyer
managerial_implications: Rich observational data and flexible machine learning can still fail to recover experimental advertising effects. The comparison with many randomized studies cautions against treating adjusted associations as causal returns. Use experiments or explicitly justified identification conditions when allocating advertising budgets.
agency_assessment: The paper improves causal measurement and cautions against unsupported attribution.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Optimizing User Engagement Through Adaptive Ad Sequencing
authors: Omid Rafieian
managerial_implications: Adaptive ad sequencing can improve measured ad response while accounting for dynamic trade-offs. In the reported application, gains mainly arise from response per impression rather than increased user activity. Evaluate causal validity and customer outcomes alongside engagement.
agency_assessment: Adaptive sequences can optimize influence without optimizing user goals. Include stopping, comprehension, and user-selected limits in evaluation.
evidence_basis: Full abstract in Crossref or OpenAlex metadata; preliminary interpretation

title: Combining Observational and Experimental Data to Improve Efficiency Using Imperfect Instruments
authors: George Z. Gui
managerial_implications: Experimental and observational data can be combined to improve precision under specified moment restrictions, even when candidate instruments violate conventional exclusion. Managers should preserve the experimental identification basis and check the assumptions linking the data sources.
agency_assessment: This estimation method does not establish a consumer-agency mechanism.
evidence_basis: Abstract in the retrieved full-text version; methods and results not exhaustively assessed

title: Frontiers: The Interplay of User-Generated Content, Content Industry Revenues, and Platform Regulation: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from YouTube
authors: Nils Wlömert; Dominik Papies; Michel Clement; Martin Spann
managerial_implications: User-generated music availability can stimulate demand for many songs while cannibalizing prominent recent releases. Aggregate revenue effects can differ from the typical song's outcome. Licensing and platform decisions should account for this distribution rather than apply a uniform policy.
